binary: rustc

cmake version 4.4.1

CMake suite maintained and supported by Kitware (kitware.com/cmake).

not_measured: DXGI adapter LUID, dedicated/shared memory budget and D3D11 feature level
DisplayConfig identity, physical origins, per-monitor DPI and WebView rasterization scale
WebView underlay/DOM layering, pointer capture and layout alignment
Spout SDK enumeration, GPU sharing, resize/restart and adapter compatibility
Frame timing, readback/copy behavior, resource retirement and device recovery

exclusions: Per-texture residency and physical allocation lifetimes
COM release does not prove driver allocation retirement
Logical BGRA bytes exclude alignment, compression and driver-private allocations
Context fences do not measure the DXGI/DWM display queue or imported source allocation ownership
Raw DXGI statistics do not prove scanout; multi-monitor reliability is unqualified and DwmFlush is not used

unqualified: texture residency, displayed cadence and latency
hardware device removal and sustained retirement

observed_outcomes: 32 native keyboard/mouse inputs plus one supported activation restore on the 100-percent secondary display, beyond three setup actions.
DOM menu/modal/native selector cover underlying native pixels; controls receive input.

Both source handles release outside their original previews; subsequent drags and controls work. Source A was clipped beyond the left viewport and recovered through its partially visible handle after window restore.
Settled native content follows docking, stage scroll, window restore/maximize and WebView zoom; no physical one-pixel accuracy claim.
Final UI and retained native status agree on layout/rendered revision 63 and host/browser scale 1.0.
limitations: Interactive capture does not qualify cadence, input-to-visible latency, physical scanout, full alpha/color cards or resource budgets.

Immediate screenshots during move/resize/zoom sometimes captured compositor transitions or the previous native position; conclusions use later settled observations. No transition-latency pass is inferred.

The terminal omitted the middle of the long native report. Complete header, observer report and footer were decoded separately from intact portions; source reports, renderer generations and full renderer resource series are unavailable from this capture.
The separate eight-second runner control proves the interactive capture/compaction route, not a reconstruction of the missing long-run rows or a repeat of the gestures.
OS 150/200-percent scaling, negative monitor origins, physical-pixel alignment, disconnected/busy editor measurements and repeated release/displayed-frame qualification remain open.
